info.name: Guild Service (Team 14)
info.description:
Guild identity, membership, roles and real-time guild chat.

Owner: IsStephy. Default port: 8087.

Every request goes through the gateway in the shared stack: the gateway verifies the player's token, drops it, and forwards `X-Gateway-Key` (proving the request came through it) plus `X-User-Id` (the player). This service never verifies tokens and answers 401 to anything without a valid `X-Gateway-Key`, except /health and /docs.

This collection talks to the service directly, so it sends those two headers itself - it plays the gateway. Set the `gatewayKey` variable to the GATEWAY_KEY in your .env (the default, `change_me`, matches .env.example). To go through the real gateway with real logins, use collections/gateway.postman_collection.json.

Guild roles are checked by this service against its own data. `GET /guilds/{guildId}` also accepts Monster Raid's `X-Service-Key` instead of a player (set `monsterRaidServiceKey` to SERVICE_KEY_MONSTER_RAID).

Run the requests top to bottom: `Create Guild` saves the new guildId, so every later request works without copy-pasting anything.

The WebSocket chat endpoint cannot be stored in Postman's collection file format; see the `Guild Chat (WebSocket)` folder for how to open it in the app.

Lab 4: the `Message Broker (Lab 4)` folder plays the Message Broker - it sends `X-Broker-Key` (set the `brokerKey` variable to BROKER_KEY in your .env; the default `change_me` matches .env.example). It needs a service started with BROKER_KEY set.

item.name: Message Broker (Lab 4)
item.description: Calls and events as the Message Broker delivers them. The broker passes on the sender's headers and adds X-Broker-Key; a call with only that key is a service's, and POST /events is where subscribed topics arrive (at least once, deduplicated by messageId).

item.name: Monster Raid reads a guild through the broker (200)

request.description: A service's call delivered by the broker: X-Broker-Key plus the caller's own X-Service-Key, and no gateway key. Accepted (#182: the broker key replaces the gateway key for service calls).

item.name: Broker-only call cannot act as a player (401)

exec: pm.test('no player', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().error).to.eql('this endpoint requires a player'); });

request.description: Every service sends the broker key, so a call with only the broker key is a service's: its X-User-Id is dropped, and a player-only endpoint answers 401.

item.name: Event delivered by the broker (200, ignored)

request.description: What the Message Broker does when Guild Service is subscribed to a topic: POST /events with the envelope and X-Broker-Key. The messageId is new on every run ({{$guid}}). Guild Service handles no topic yet, so it acknowledges the event as "ignored" - and records the messageId.
The broker delivers at least once: a copy whose acknowledgement got lost comes again. The messageId is already in handled_messages, so it is acknowledged without being handled twice.
Only the broker delivers events: even the gateway's key is not enough.

item.name: Event that is not an envelope (400)

exec: pm.test('names what is missing', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().error).to.eql('messageId is required'); });

request.description: No messageId: delivering it again would not fix it, so 400.

item.name: Guild Chat (WebSocket)
item.description:
`WS /guilds/{guildId}/chat` - real-time guild chat.

Postman's collection file format (v2.1) cannot store WebSocket requests, so open it inside the Postman app.

The socket needs a single-use ticket from the gateway - the chat checks it instead of a user token:

1. Through the gateway, as a logged-in player (see collections/gateway.postman_collection.json):
   GET http://localhost:8080/ws/negotiate?path=/guilds/<guildId>/chat
   Authorization: Bearer <token>
   -> { "wsUrl": "ws://localhost:8087/guilds/<guildId>/chat?ticket=<ticket>" }
2. New -> WebSocket Request, URL: the wsUrl from step 1. Connect within 60 seconds - the ticket expires, and opens one socket only.
3. The server immediately sends the existing history:
   { "type": "history", "messages": [] }
4. Send this JSON message, with authorId = the player you logged in as:
   { "authorId": "<your userId>", "message": "hello guild" }
5. The server stamps it and broadcasts it to every connected member:
   { "authorId": "<your userId>", "message": "hello guild", "timestamp": "2026-10-06T12:11:03.692Z" }

Rules: a missing, expired, reused or wrong-path ticket, an unknown guild, or a caller who is not a member closes the socket with 1008; too many open sockets close it with 1013. authorId must be the ticket's player.

To demonstrate the broadcast, negotiate twice (one ticket per socket) and send from one of the two tabs.
